w-kr-018.title: Korean Potato Side Dish (Gamja Jorim)

instructions.1: Rinse the potatoes. If using thick-skinned potatoes, peel and cut them into cubes.
instructions.2: Place the potatoes in a pot with enough water to fully cover them. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium and cook for about 10 minutes. Drain the potatoes.
instructions.3: Return the potatoes to the pot and add 2 cups of water, 3 tablespoons of soy sauce, sugar, vegetable oil, and the dried shiitake mushroom (if using). Bring to a boil, then simmer, covered, for about 30 minutes or until the liquid has reduced to one-third.
instructions.4: Uncover the pot, add 2 tablespoons of maple syrup. Continue to cook until the liquid has almost completely reduced. Taste and add more soy sauce if desired (up to 1 teaspoon).
instructions.5: Stir the potatoes for a few more minutes. Finish the dish with a swirl of sesame oil and a sprinkling of sesame seeds.

w-kr-018.culturalNotes: Gamja Jorim is a traditional Korean side dish, typically served with rice.

w-kr-019.title: Quick Kimchi

instructions.1: Rinse the napa cabbage well and cut an 'X' into the root end, going about 3 inches deep.
instructions.2: Pull apart at the 'X' to easily divide the cabbage into four equal segments.
instructions.3: Cut away the tough core and chop the cabbage into bite-sized pieces. Place in a large bowl, sprinkle with salt, and let sit for 2-3 hours, tossing occasionally.
instructions.4: While the cabbage is sitting, grate the ginger and garlic and cut the green onion into large pieces.
instructions.5: Measure out the red pepper powder and shrimp paste. You could easily double the red pepper for a fiery hot kimchi.
instructions.6: Drain the cabbage, pressing it through a colander, and return it to the mixing bowl. Stir together with the rest of the ingredients until evenly distributed.
instructions.7: Place the kimchi in an airtight container and let it sit on the counter for 2-3 days.
instructions.8: Everything will soften up, the juices will release, and it’ll be ready for nibbling. Refrigerate and use as desired. The kimchi will keep for a couple of weeks in the refrigerator.

w-kr-019.culturalNotes: Kimchi is a traditional Korean dish served with most meals. It is typically made from napa cabbage, green onions, garlic, and ginger.

w-kr-020.title: Korean Spicy Cold Noodles (Bibim Guksu)

instructions.1: Cook the thin dry Korean noodles in 5 cups of water until tender, then drain and rinse with cold water.
instructions.2: Peel the egg and slice it thinly.
instructions.3: In a small bowl, mix the grated apple, grated onion, minced garlic, rice vinegar, gochujang, gochukaru, soy sauce, sugar, honey, sesame oil, and soup soy sauce.
instructions.4: In another bowl, mix the sliced Korean radish, Korean sea salt, rice vinegar, and sugar.
instructions.5: In a serving bowl, place the noodles, then add the sliced egg, bibim sauce, sliced vegetables, and kimchi.
instructions.6: Gently toss the ingredients until well combined.
instructions.7: Serve the dish cold, garnished with red leaf lettuce and perilla leaves.

w-kr-020.culturalNotes: Bibim Guksu is a popular dish in Korea, typically served in the summer to enjoy its refreshing coolness.

w-kr-021.title: Pickled Yellow Radish (Danmuji) - Korean Style

instructions.1: Clean and sanitize the pickling jar by washing it with soap, rinsing it, and boiling it in a pot of hot water. If you are going to store it in the fridge, you can skip the boiling step and just use a dishwasher to clean the jar.
instructions.2: Clean the Korean radish (Mu) and brush the outer skin with a vegetable brush if the radish is fresh and clean enough to use the skin. If the skin is blemished or has black spots, it's best to peel the skin.
instructions.3: Cut the radish into 1/4 inch thick slices or into logs that will fit into the jar.
instructions.4: In a small pot, add 250 ml of water, 1/2 cup of sugar, 1 Tbsp of Korean sea salt, and 1/4 cup of rice vinegar to make the pickling juice.
instructions.5: Simmer the ingredients in the pot until all the seasoning has dissolved in the water.
instructions.6: While the pickling liquid is simmering, cut the radish into thin 1/4 inch slices or into chunks small enough to fit into your jar.
instructions.7: In the clean jar, pack in the radish and pour the hot pickling juice along with 3 pods of dried gardenia fruit (chija). Try to place the gardenia fruit well at the bottom for the whole jar to become evenly yellow.
instructions.8: Leave it in the jar for about a week until the radish starts to look a bit shriveled. Swirl it a couple of times so the gardenia fruit colors the radishes evenly.

w-kr-021.culturalNotes: Danmuji is a traditional Korean dish served as a side dish or with rice. It is known for its distinctive yellow color and sweet-sour taste.

w-kr-022.title: Tteok Mandu Guk (Rice Cake Soup with Dumplings)

w-kr-022-i9.name: 1/2 sheet gim nori, cut into thin strips

instructions.1: Cut the beef into thin bite-size pieces (1-1.5 inches).
instructions.2: In a medium pot, sauté the beef with 1 tablespoon of soup soy sauce until all the pieces turn brown. Pour in 5 cups of water and bring it to a boil. Skim off the foam. Reduce the heat to medium and continue to boil, covered, for 10 minutes.
instructions.3: You can add the dumplings to the soup along with the rice cakes in the next step. Another option is to cook the dumplings separately in the boiling water until the dumplings float to the top, and then add to the soup when the rice cakes are cooked. Or, line a steamer with a wet cheesecloth and then steam mandu for about 8 minutes (10 minutes if frozen).
instructions.4: Add the garlic and the rice cake slices to the boiling broth. Boil until the rice cakes turn very soft, usually about 5-8 minutes.
instructions.5: Drop the cooked dumplings and the scallion into the soup. Let the soup come to a boil again. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Ladle the steaming soup into individual bowls and garnish with the optional egg and gim strips.

w-kr-022.culturalNotes: Tteok Mandu Guk is a popular dish in South Korea, often served on special occasions.

w-kr-023.title: Brown Rice and Pumpkin Porridge (Hyunmi Danhobak Mium)

instructions.1: Wash the brown rice and soak it in water for 30 minutes. Drain the water after 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Wash, cut, and peel the pumpkin. Steam it in a boiling pot until it is cooked (20 to 25 minutes). It can be quicker if the pumpkin is chopped thinner and smaller.
instructions.3: Add the rice, steamed pumpkin, and water to a blender and blend for 1 to 2 minutes.
instructions.4: Pour the mixture into a small pot and bring it to a boil over high heat for 2 minutes. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
instructions.5: Sieve the boiled porridge. (Discard what is left on the sieve).
instructions.6: Cool it down for 10 to 20 minutes, then serve it (or distribute it among pre-portioned containers for later consumption).

w-kr-023.culturalNotes: This porridge is a traditional Korean dish served to newborns and patients to aid in their recovery.

w-kr-024.title: Korean Seaweed Soup (Miyeok Guk)

w-kr-024-i2.name: beef
w-kr-024-i2.standardAmount: 120 g (4.2 ounces), sliced into smaller pieces

instructions.1: Soak the dried seaweed in cold water for 5 to 10 minutes until it expands. Drain the water and rinse the seaweed a couple of times in running water. Drain and squeeze out the water. If you’re using non pre-cut dried seaweed, cut it with scissors into pieces about the size of your little finger. Set it aside.
instructions.2: Combine the sliced beef with the salt and black pepper in a small bowl. Mix them well and set aside until needed.
instructions.3: Preheat a medium pot over medium heat for about 20 seconds. Add the sesame oil, seaweed, and beef. Stir them well until the beef is partly cooked (about 2 minutes).
instructions.4: Add the soy sauce, garlic, and water. Cover the pot and boil over medium to medium-high heat until the meat is fully cooked (10 to 15 minutes). Adjust the taste with more salt if needed.
instructions.5: Serve the soup warm with a bowl of steamed rice and other Korean side dishes.

w-kr-024.culturalNotes: Korean seaweed soup (Miyeok Guk) is a traditional dish served on special occasions, especially on a child's birthday.

w-kr-025.title: Naengmyeon (Korean Cold Noodle Soup)

instructions.1: Make the beef broth: Place the beef, garlic, ginger, onion, and water in a pot. Simmer for two hours. Strain the broth and add the Korean soup soy sauce, sea salt, cucumber pickle liquid, and radish pickle liquid. Let it cool.
instructions.2: Pickle the cucumber: Slice the cucumber thinly and add the salt, rice vinegar, and sugar. Mix well and let it sit for 10 minutes.
instructions.3: Pickle the radish: Slice the radish thinly and add the salt, rice vinegar, and sugar. Mix well and let it sit for 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Boil the eggs: Place the eggs in boiling water for 10 minutes. Rinse with cold water and peel them.
instructions.5: Peel and slice the Asian pear: Peel the Asian pear and slice it thinly.
instructions.6: Cook the noodles: Boil water in a pot and add the noodles. Boil for 5 minutes or according to package instructions. Drain the noodles and rinse with cold water.
instructions.7: Serve the naengmyeon: Place the noodles in serving bowls, add the cold broth, pickled cucumber, pickled radish, boiled eggs, and slices of Asian pear.

w-kr-025.culturalNotes: Naengmyeon is a traditional Korean dish served in the summer to enjoy its refreshing coolness.

w-kr-026.title: Ssukgat Namul (Chrysanthemum Greens)

instructions.1: Start boiling 6 cups of water with 1 tsp of salt.
instructions.2: Wash and clean the chrysanthemum greens in water and drain.
instructions.3: Cut the bottom stem part into 2-inch lengths and the upper leafy parts into 4-5 inch lengths.
instructions.4: Chop the green onions and prepare an ice bath (a bowl of cold water + a bowl of ice) to put the blanched chrysanthemum leaves in.
instructions.5: Once the water starts boiling in the pot, add just the stem parts first and cook for 1 minute or so. Then add the rest of the leaves and cook for another 1-2 minutes until the thickest stems are cooked.
instructions.6: When it's cooked, quickly remove the pot from heat and transfer the cooked chrysanthemum leaves into the ice bath. Let it cool then remove the leaves from the ice bath and put into a colander.
instructions.7: Then take a handful of it between your hands and squeeze out excess water from the cooked greens. Gently squeeze but don't wring it totally out.
instructions.8: In a bowl, add the balls of squeezed greens and loosen them so the leaves are loosely separated. Now, add the green onions and seasonings - Guk Ganjang, sea salt, sesame seeds, and sesame oil. Use your hands (use gloves if you want) to gently massage all the seasonings into the greens. Once it's all nicely mixed, taste and adjust if necessary.
instructions.9: Serve at room temperature or cold from the fridge with any Korean dish.

w-kr-026.culturalNotes: Ssukgat Namul is a traditional Korean side dish served with many Korean dishes. It is known for its fresh flavor and slightly crunchy texture.

w-kr-027.title: Korean Radish Salad (Moosaengche)

instructions.1: Wash and peel the Korean radish.
instructions.2: Julienne the radish to make about 6 cups.
instructions.3: Put the julienned radish into a large bowl and sprinkle with sea salt. Toss the radish pieces to distribute the salt evenly.
instructions.4: Add the rice vinegar, sugar, and Korean red pepper powder. You can add more or less to taste.

w-kr-027.culturalNotes: This Korean radish salad, known as Moosaengche, is served as an appetizer in Korean meals.

w-kr-028.title: Ssamjang

w-kr-028-i8.name: walnuts (or your choice of nuts and seeds)

w-kr-028-i9.name: apple, cored and cut into small pieces

instructions.1: Add all ingredients to a food processor and blend until smooth. This will take about 1 minute.
instructions.2: Transfer the sauce to a serving bowl.
instructions.3: Garnish with green onion and sesame seeds if desired.

w-kr-028.culturalNotes: Ssamjang is a traditional Korean sauce used as a filling for fresh vegetables or grilled meats.

w-kr-029.title: Sujebi (Korean Hand-Pulled Noodle Soup)

w-kr-029-i3.name: water
w-kr-029-i3.standardAmount: 160 ml (add 1-2 tsp more if you didn't exact weigh your flour)

w-kr-029-i7.name: Korean sea salt
w-kr-029-i7.standardAmount: 1.5 tsp (use less if it's not Korean sea salt, also use 1 tsp if using yangnyeomjang later)

w-kr-029-i8.name: Korean soup soy sauce (guk ganjang)
w-kr-029-i8.standardAmount: 1.25 tsp (reduce to 1 tsp if using yangnyeomjang)

w-kr-029-i16.name: red chili pepper (chopped)
w-kr-029-i16.standardAmount: 2 tsp (substitute shishito peppers (double amount) if you want mild sauce, adjust to your spice level)

instructions.1: Prepare the dough: In a large bowl, mix the flour and salt. Gradually add the water and knead until the dough is smooth. Cover the dough and let it rest for 15 minutes.
instructions.2: Prepare the broth: In a large pot, bring 6 cups of water to a boil over medium heat. Add the dried anchovies and dried kelp, and simmer for 20 minutes. Strain the broth and remove the anchovies and kelp.
instructions.3: Prepare the vegetables: Cut the potato, yellow onion, and Korean aehobak or Italian zucchini into small cubes. Slice the green onions thinly.
instructions.4: Prepare the sauce (optional): In a small bowl, mix the minced garlic, regular soy sauce, Korean red chili powder, chopped red chili pepper, rice vinegar, oil, sugar, black pepper, and sesame seeds.
instructions.5: Prepare the soup: In a large pot, bring the broth to a boil. Add the potato, yellow onion, and Korean aehobak or Italian zucchini, and simmer for 10 minutes. Add the Korean sea salt and Korean soup soy sauce, and stir well.
instructions.6: Prepare the noodles: Cut the dough into small pieces, then stretch them between your hands to form the noodles. Add the noodles to the soup and simmer for 5 minutes.
instructions.7: Serve the soup: Ladle the soup into serving bowls, garnish with chopped green onions and the sauce (if prepared), and serve hot.

w-kr-029.culturalNotes: Sujebi is a traditional Korean soup made with hand-pulled noodles and vegetables. It is typically served in a large bowl and contains a rich, flavorful broth.

w-kr-030.title: Sundubu-jjigae (Korean Spicy Soft Tofu Stew)

w-kr-030-i8.name: dried kelp and dried anchovy stock

instructions.1: Start heating the pot on the stove over medium low heat and add the chili oil, chili powder, and garlic. Stir them well for about 1 min. Make sure not to burn the chili powder.
instructions.2: Add the clams and shrimps and stir quickly to coat them with the chili sauce. Add the fish sauce and soy sauce then stir.
instructions.3: Add the dried kelp and anchovy stock and boil it on medium-high heat until it starts to boil rapidly (2 to 3 mins).
instructions.4: Add the tofu, mushrooms, and egg and cook them for another 2 to 3 mins. Season with salt, if required.
instructions.5: Top up with the green onion, black pepper, and sesame oil. Serve hot with Korean rice and side dishes (banchan).

w-kr-030.culturalNotes: Sundubu-jjigae is a traditional Korean stew often served in a hot iron pot, and it is an important part of Korean cuisine.

w-kr-031.title: Tteokbokki

instructions.1: Make Kelp broth - soak dried kelp (Dasima or Kombu) in hot water for at least 10 minutes. Using plain water is okay but it won't be as flavorful.
instructions.2: Prepare Rice Cakes - If you have fresh or refrigerated rice cakes, just pull them apart so they are all separated. If your tteok is frozen, defrost by soaking it in cold water for a few minutes and then drain.
instructions.3: Pour kelp broth (or water) into a pan. Add tteok (rice cakes) and turn heat on medium high and bring to boil.
instructions.4: Add Tteokbokki Sauce - you can premix the sauce in a bowl first or you can just add Gochujang, sugar, soy sauce, garlic powder or chopped garlic directly and mix in the pan.
instructions.5: Once it starts to boil, lower heat to simmer and let it reduce for 10-13 minutes, depending on how thick you want the sauce to be.
instructions.6: Sprinkle some chopped green onions, sesame seeds, and a swirl of sesame oil (if desired). Enjoy!

w-kr-031.culturalNotes: Tteokbokki is a popular dish in South Korea, served as a snack or main meal. It is known for its spicy and sweet flavor.

w-kr-032.title: Korean Rice Cake Soup (Tteokguk)

instructions.1: If using frozen rice cakes, soak them in water for 10 minutes and drain. If using fresh rice cakes, rinse them quickly with water and drain.
instructions.2: Cut the onion in half and use half of it (not cut) for the broth. Slice the remaining half into thin slices to be added later.
instructions.3: Peel the garlic cloves and use some of them whole for the broth and chop the rest.
instructions.4: Add the beef, the uncut half of the onion, and the water to the Instant Pot. Close the lid and set the valve to sealing. Set the Instant Pot to the Soup setting and cook for 20 minutes.
instructions.5: After the cooking time, carefully release the pressure. Add the rice cakes, sliced onion, chopped garlic, soy sauce, sea salt, sugar, and black pepper. Mix the ingredients well.
instructions.6: Re-set the Instant Pot to the Soup setting for 10 minutes.
instructions.7: After the cooking time, carefully release the pressure. Add the sliced green onions, roasted seaweed, and beaten egg. Gently mix the ingredients.
instructions.8: Serve the soup hot, garnished with roasted seaweed and sliced green onions.

w-kr-032.culturalNotes: Korean Rice Cake Soup (tteokguk) is a traditional dish served on Korean New Year's Day.

w-kr-033.title: Yukgaejang - Korean Spicy Beef Soup

instructions.1: Soak the beef brisket in cold water for 5-10 minutes to draw out the blood, then rinse it well.
instructions.2: Peel the onion and garlic cloves.
instructions.3: In the Instant Pot or pressure cooker, add water, beef brisket, whole onion, and whole garlic cloves.
instructions.4: Cover the pot and select the Meat/Stew function and set the time to 30 minutes.
instructions.5: After the time is up, remove the beef brisket and cut it into small pieces.
instructions.6: In a bowl, mix the Korean red chili pepper, Korean Soup Soy Sauce, sea salt, Gochujang, sugar, chopped garlic, garlic powder, and ground black pepper.
instructions.7: Return the beef to the pot and add the spice mixture.
instructions.8: Add the green onions, mung bean sprouts, eggs, and Korean leek.
instructions.9: Re-cover the pot and cook for 10 minutes on low pressure.
instructions.10: After the time is up, remove the pot from heat and add the crushed sesame seeds and sesame oil.
instructions.11: Serve the soup hot with rice if desired.

w-kr-033.culturalNotes: Yukgaejang is a traditional Korean spicy beef soup, often served on special occasions and during the winter.

w-in-001.title: Kajjaya (Adhirasam)

instructions.1: Wash the rice and soak it in water for 4 hours.
instructions.2: Drain the rice and let it dry for 12 hours.
instructions.3: Grind the rice with sesame seeds and poppy seeds until smooth, then mix the ingredients well.
instructions.4: Dissolve the jaggery in water and strain it to remove impurities.
instructions.5: Add the dissolved jaggery to the rice mixture and knead the dough.
instructions.6: Let the dough rest for 30 minutes.
instructions.7: Shape the dough into small discs.
instructions.8: Fry the discs in oil or ghee until golden brown.
instructions.9: Drain the fried discs on paper towels.

w-in-001.culturalNotes: Kajjaya is a traditional Indian sweet served on special occasions and celebrations.

w-in-002.title: Aloo Chop

instructions.1: First, to prepare the masala for the chop, dry roast 1 tsp cumin, 1 tbsp coriander seeds, and 3 dried red chilli on low flame until the spices become aromatic.
instructions.2: Cool completely, and grind to a fine powder. Keep aside.
instructions.3: In a bowl, take 1.5 cups besan, 1/4 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp chilli powder, and 1/2 tsp salt.
instructions.4: Add water as needed to prepare a smooth batter. Keep aside.
instructions.5: To prepare the stuffing, mash 3 boiled potatoes and keep aside.
instructions.6: In a pan, heat 2 tbsp oil. Add 1/2 tsp cumin and a pinch of hing.
instructions.7: Add 2 chilli, 1/2 onion, 1 tsp ginger garlic paste, and sauté well.
instructions.8: On low flame, add 1/2 tsp turmeric, 2 boiled potatoes, 1/2 tsp salt, and mix well.
instructions.9: Add the prepared masala powder, 2 tbsp coriander, 1/2 tsp kala namak, and mix well.
instructions.10: Once the stuffing is cooled completely, prepare small patty-shaped mixture. Keep aside.
instructions.11: To the besan batter, add 1/4 tsp baking soda and mix well just before frying.
instructions.12: Dip the aloo mixture in besan batter coating the batter uniformly.
instructions.13: Deep fry in hot oil, keeping the flame on medium. Stir occasionally, and fry on both sides until crispy and golden brown. Drain off.
instructions.14: Finally, enjoy Aloo Chop with chutney.

w-in-002.culturalNotes: Aloo Chop is a popular dish in Bangladesh and India, served as an appetizer or a light snack.

w-in-003.title: Aloo Gobhi (Dry)

instructions.1: In a large kadai, heat 3 tbsp of oil and add 1 tsp of cumin and kasuri methi, sauté until aromatic.
instructions.2: Add finely chopped onion and sauté well until golden.
instructions.3: Add ginger garlic paste and slit chilli, sauté for a minute.
instructions.4: Add turmeric, Kashmiri red chilli powder, cumin powder, and salt, sauté on low flame until the spices become aromatic.
instructions.5: Add finely chopped tomato and sauté until the tomatoes turn soft and mushy.
instructions.6: Add fried potatoes and cauliflower, mix gently without breaking them.
instructions.7: If you prefer gravy, add ½ cup of water.
instructions.8: Add aamchur, garam masala, and chopped coriander leaves, mix well.
instructions.9: Serve the dish with roti or rice.

w-in-003.culturalNotes: Aloo Gobhi is a popular Indian dish, typically served with roti or rice.

w-in-004.title: Aloo Tikki

instructions.1: Mix the mashed potatoes, boiled peas, and spices in a bowl.
instructions.2: Shape the potato mixture into round patties.
instructions.3: Dip the patties in the flour mixture and coat them with breadcrumbs.
instructions.4: Fry the patties in hot oil until they turn golden and crispy.
instructions.5: Cut the burger buns in half and spread a teaspoon of burger sauce on each side.
instructions.6: Place lettuce leaves on the bottom half of the bun, followed by the aloo tikki.
instructions.7: Spread a teaspoon of burger sauce on the aloo tikki.
instructions.8: Place slices of tomato and onion rings on the aloo tikki.
instructions.9: Cover the aloo tikki with the top half of the bun and press slightly.
instructions.10: Serve the burger with French fries.

w-in-004.culturalNotes: Aloo Tikki is a popular dish in India, often served as an appetizer or a light meal.

w-in-005.title: Baingan Bharta

instructions.1: Take a large-sized eggplant and make 4 slits.
instructions.2: Stuff 3 cloves of garlic and 1 chili into each slit.
instructions.3: Grease the eggplant with oil to help peel the skin off easily after roasting.
instructions.4: Roast the eggplant on the gas stove, flipping occasionally until it turns dark and is cooked completely from the inside.
instructions.5: Let the eggplant cool completely, then peel the skin off and remove the head.
instructions.6: Mash the eggplant with a fork and set aside.
instructions.7: In a large kadai, heat 2 tablespoons of oil and sauté 1 teaspoon of cumin, 1 dried red chili, 1 inch of ginger, and 3 cloves of garlic.
instructions.8: Sauté the onion until it shrinks slightly.
instructions.9: Add ½ teaspoon of Kashmiri red chili powder, 1 teaspoon of coriander powder, and sauté until the spices become aromatic.
instructions.10: Add the tomato and sauté until it becomes soft and mushy.
instructions.11: Add the roasted and mashed eggplant, 1 teaspoon of salt, and mix for 5 minutes until the flavors are well combined.
instructions.12: Add ½ teaspoon of garam masala and 2 tablespoons of fresh coriander, and mix well.
instructions.13: Serve the baingan bharta hot with phulka or rice.

w-in-005.culturalNotes: Baingan Bharta is a popular dish in India, known for its rich and smoky flavors.

w-in-006.title: Basundi

instructions.1: First, crumble 100 grams of khova and keep it aside. If you don't have khova, you can use ½ cup of milk powder.
instructions.2: In a large kadai, take 1.5 litres of milk and bring it to a boil, stirring occasionally.
instructions.3: Add 2 tablespoons of kesar milk and mix well.
instructions.4: Boil for 5 minutes, or until the milk thickens slightly.
instructions.5: Once the milk reduces, add the crumbled khova and mix well.
instructions.6: Continue to boil for 5 more minutes or until the milk thickens.
instructions.7: Add ¼ cup of sugar and bring it to a boil. Make sure the sugar is dissolved well.
instructions.8: Add ½ teaspoon of cardamom powder and 2 tablespoons of chopped almonds. Mix well.
instructions.9: Let the basundi cool slightly before serving. The basundi will thicken once cooled.
instructions.10: Finally, enjoy the basundi chilled or warm, and it can be stored in the refrigerator for a week.

w-in-006.culturalNotes: Basundi is a traditional Indian sweet usually served on special occasions.

w-in-007.title: Bati (Bread)

instructions.1: Mix the flour and salt in a bowl.
instructions.2: Add about 1 cup of the flour mixture to a small bowl and add a little oil, mixing it in well and breaking up any lumps.
instructions.3: Add water about 1 tablespoon at a time and keep kneading with your hands. You only need 3-4 tablespoons, but you must knead the dough very hard to make it stick together in a ball.
instructions.4: Let the balls sit for 5 minutes.
instructions.5: Flatten out each ball with first your hands and then a rolling pin until they are smooth discs 4 inches (10 cm) across and ½ inch (1.25 cm) thick.
instructions.6: Cook in a dry metal pan on a low flame. Flip once when the bottom begins to harden, then pinch all over with two fingers so the dough is not too thick and has a bumpy texture on one side.
instructions.7: Check the bottom until it browns in spots, then remove the baati and place it upside-down on a grate or pan with holes in it. This will blacken the top a little, especially on the tops of the pinched bumps.
instructions.8: Serve with ghee and a dhal or vegetable.

w-in-007.culturalNotes: Bati is a traditional bread in India, especially in the state of Rajasthan. It is usually served with ghee and lentils or vegetables.

w-in-008.title: Benne Dose

instructions.1: First, blend 1 cup of soaked urad dal in a blender with water as needed until it becomes a smooth paste.
instructions.2: Transfer the smooth and fluffy batter of urad dal into a large bowl.
instructions.3: In the blender, blend 3 cups of dosa rice and 1/2 tsp of fenugreek seeds to a slightly coarse paste with water as needed.
instructions.4: Transfer the rice batter to the bowl of urad dal batter.
instructions.5: Take 2 cups of washed and squeezed puffed rice and place it in the blender.
instructions.6: Blend it to a smooth paste.
instructions.7: Mix everything well to ensure everything is combined thoroughly.
instructions.8: Cover and rest the batter in a warm place for 8-10 hours or until it ferments and doubles in size.
instructions.9: Add 1.5 tsp of salt to the batter and mix well.
instructions.10: Heat the griddle and pour a ladleful of batter.
instructions.11: Spread the batter in a circular motion slightly thicker than a regular masala dosa.
instructions.12: Spread a tsp of oil from the sides of the dosa.
instructions.13: Add 1 tbsp of butter and spread it on all sides of the dosa.
instructions.14: Roast the dosa to a golden brown on both sides.
instructions.15: Finally, fold the benne dose / butter dosa into half and serve with chutney and aloo bhaji topped with more butter.

w-in-008.culturalNotes: Benne Dose is a popular dish in the Indian state of Karnataka, known for its rich and delicious flavor thanks to the butter.

w-in-009.title: Spinach Bhaji

instructions.1: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
instructions.2: Add the green chili peppers and toast for 2 minutes.
instructions.3: Add the onion and cook until soft.
instructions.4: Add the garlic and panch phoron. The spices will start to pop and crackle when ready.
instructions.5: Add the spinach, salt, and pepper. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes, allowing all the flavors to meld.

w-in-009.culturalNotes: Bhaji is a popular dish in India, often served as part of a lunch or dinner meal.

w-in-010.title: Bhel Puri

instructions.1: In hot oil, place a sieve and fry ½ cup peanuts on low flame until they become crunchy. Drain and set aside.
instructions.2: Now fry ½ cup roasted gram dal on low flame until it turns crunchy. Drain and set aside.
instructions.3: Also, fry ¾ cup thick poha in hot oil until the poha turns crispy. Drain and set aside.
instructions.4: In a large kadai, heat 2 tbsp oil. Add ½ tsp turmeric, ½ tsp chilli powder, a pinch of hing, and a few curry leaves.
instructions.5: Saute on low flame until the spices turn aromatic.
instructions.6: Add 4 cups murmura and fry until the murmura turns crispy and the spices are well combined.
instructions.7: Turn off the flame and add ½ tsp cumin powder, 1 tsp chaat masala, ½ tsp kala namak, ½ tsp salt, 2 tbsp powdered sugar, and ½ tsp aamchur.
instructions.8: Add ½ cup spicy boondi, ½ cup sev, crush 10 papdi and mix well.
instructions.9: Mix well making sure all are well combined.
instructions.10: Finally, Bhel Puri Mix is ready to make chaat.
instructions.11: To make Bhel Puri Chaat: Place the mix in serving dishes, add ½ cup finely chopped onion, ½ cup finely chopped tomato, ½ cup cubed boiled potato, ½ tsp chaat masala, 2 tbsp green chutney, 2 tbsp tamarind chutney, 2 finely chopped chilli, 2 tbsp chopped coriander, and juice of ½ lemon. Mix well and serve.

w-in-010.culturalNotes: Bhel Puri is a popular street food in India, especially in Mumbai, and is served as chaat in public places and streets.

w-in-011.title: Chicken Biryani

instructions.1: Wash the rice and soak it for 30 minutes, then drain and cook it.
instructions.2: Marinate the chicken in a mixture of lemon juice, yoghurt, ginger, garlic, salt, turmeric powder, cumin powder, cloves, chillies, chopped tomatoes, and tomato purée.
instructions.3: Heat the oil in a pan, add the onions, and cook until golden brown, then add them to the chicken.
instructions.4: Grease a heavy-bottomed deep and wide-mouthed pan, then add a layer of rice, followed by the chicken mixture, and top with the remaining rice and saffron.
instructions.5: Bake the biryani in the oven for 1-1.5 hours at 150°C (300°F). Check to ensure the chicken is cooked through.
instructions.6: Serve the biryani with yoghurt on the side.

w-in-011.culturalNotes: Biryani is a popular dish in India, known for its rich blend of spices and flavors.

w-in-012.title: Bonda (Snack)

instructions.1: In a large kadai, heat the oil and add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, crushed coriander seeds, asafoetida, and curry leaves. Allow to splutter.
instructions.2: Add the broken cashews and roast until golden.
instructions.3: Add the chopped onion, ginger, and green chilli. Sauté until the onion turns golden.
instructions.4: Add turmeric, Kashmiri red chilli powder, coriander leaves, and salt. Sauté for a minute.
instructions.5: Add the mashed potato, coriander leaves, and lemon juice. Mix well.
instructions.6: Shape the potato mixture into balls.
instructions.7: Prepare the batter by mixing gram flour, corn flour, water, and baking soda until you get a thick batter.
instructions.8: Dip the balls in the batter and deep fry in hot oil until golden and crisp.
instructions.9: Serve the bonda with chutney or tomato sauce.

w-in-012.culturalNotes: Bonda is a popular snack in India, especially in South India, and is typically served as a snack or appetizer.

w-in-013.title: Aloo Stuffed Bread Pakora

instructions.1: In a large mixing bowl, place the mashed potatoes.
instructions.2: Add the green chilli, ginger, coriander, Kashmiri red chilli powder, dry mango powder, chaat masala, and salt. Mix all the ingredients well to prepare the potato stuffing.
instructions.3: In another bowl, mix the gram flour, rice flour, Kashmiri red chilli powder, salt, and a pinch of soda. Gradually add water to prepare the batter.
instructions.4: Spread a teaspoon of green chutney on a bread slice and cut it in half.
instructions.5: Spread a tablespoon of the prepared potato stuffing on half of the bread slice, then cover it with another half slice.
instructions.6: Dip the piece in the batter to coat it on all sides.
instructions.7: Deep fry the piece in hot oil over medium heat, flipping occasionally until it turns golden and crispy.
instructions.8: Serve the aloo stuffed bread pakora with green chutney or tomato sauce.

w-in-013.culturalNotes: Aloo stuffed bread pakora is a popular dish in India, served as an appetizer at gatherings and in homes.

w-in-014.title: Butter Chicken

w-in-014-i1.name: Skinless, boneless chicken thighs or breasts

instructions.1: Trim and cut the chicken into small cubes. If you prefer chicken on the bone, cut long thin slices laterally into the chicken.
instructions.2: In a large bowl, combine the tandoori masala powder, yogurt, lemon juice, and chicken. Massage this well with your hands so that all the chicken is evenly covered in the tandoori masala. Cover and set aside for at least 30 minutes.
instructions.3: Heat a large saucepan or frying pan until evenly hot.
instructions.4: In the pan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter until it is frothy. Add the onions and cinnamon and fry lightly. When the onions are soft and starting to brown, stir in the crushed garlic and ginger. Then add the turmeric, chili, and coriander, and sauté over medium heat.
instructions.5: Add the chicken and sauté, stirring constantly until the chicken has turned white. This doesn't take long, so make sure you don't overcook the chicken.
instructions.6: Mix in the tomato paste. Add the cream and heat through. After adding the cream and stirring, you may add additional tandoori masala. About 3-5 tablespoons is generally sufficient.
instructions.7: Cover and simmer for just over 10 minutes.

w-in-014.culturalNotes: Butter chicken is a famous dish in Indian cuisine, typically served with basmati rice or naan.

w-in-015.title: Capsicum Rice

instructions.1: First, dry roast 2 tbsp of peanuts until they become crunchy.
instructions.2: Add 2 tbsp of sesame seeds, 1 tsp of cumin seeds, 1/2 tsp of coriander seeds, 1/2 tsp of urad dal, and 1/2 tsp of chana dal.
instructions.3: Dry roast on low flame until the spices become aromatic.
instructions.4: Cool completely, then grind to a fine powder. Keep aside.
instructions.5: In a large kadai, heat 2 tbsp of oil. Add 1 tsp of mustard seeds, 1/2 tsp of cumin seeds, 2 dried red chilli, a pinch of hing, and a few curry leaves.
instructions.6: Add 1 sliced onion and sauté slightly until the onion softens.
instructions.7: Now add 1 sliced capsicum and sauté until the capsicum becomes crunchy.
instructions.8: Further, keeping the flame on low, add 1/2 tsp of turmeric, 1 tsp of chilli powder, 1/2 tsp of garam masala, and 1 tsp of salt.
instructions.9: Sauté on low flame until the spices become aromatic.
instructions.10: Add 4 cups of cooked rice and the peanut masala.
instructions.11: Mix gently, making sure everything is well combined.
instructions.12: Cover and simmer for 5 minutes or until the spices are absorbed well.
instructions.13: Add 2 tbsp of chopped coriander and 1/2 tbsp of lemon juice, and mix well.
instructions.14: Finally, enjoy Capsicum Rice with raita.

w-in-015.culturalNotes: Capsicum Rice is a popular dish in Indian cuisine, especially in restaurants and canteens. It is usually served with raita.

w-in-016.title: Butter Murukku (Chakli)

instructions.1: In a large bowl, combine 3 cups of rice flour, ¾ cup of urad dal flour, 2 tablespoons of sesame seeds, a pinch of hing, and 1 teaspoon of salt.
instructions.2: Mix the ingredients well to ensure they are well combined.
instructions.3: Add 3 tablespoons of butter and mix well. Crumble and mix until the flour is moist.
instructions.4: Add water gradually and start kneading the dough.
instructions.5: Knead the dough until it is smooth and soft, adding water as needed.
instructions.6: Attach the star mold to the chakli maker and grease it with a little oil to prevent the dough from sticking.
instructions.7: Shape the dough into a cylindrical form and place it inside the chakli maker.
instructions.8: Close the lid and start preparing the chaklis.
instructions.9: Add the chaklis to hot oil over medium heat.
instructions.10: Flip the chaklis and fry them on medium heat until they are crispy on both sides.
instructions.11: Drain the chaklis on paper towels to remove excess oil.
instructions.12: Once cooled, enjoy the instant butter chakli or store them in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.

w-in-016.culturalNotes: Chakli is a traditional Indian sweet snack typically served during special occasions and celebrations.

w-in-017.title: Chak Chak

instructions.1: Melt the butter in a medium pot over medium heat.
instructions.2: Toss the noodles in a bit of flour and place in the pot to cook until a little crispy and golden. About 5 minutes depending on noodle thickness.
instructions.3: Melt the honey and sugar in a small saucepan over medium heat. Let the mixture bubble until all the sugar dissolves.
instructions.4: Pour the mixture over the fried noodles while still boiling. Toss to coat evenly.
instructions.5: Dip your hand in cool water and shape the noodles into domes.

w-in-017.culturalNotes: Chak Chak is a traditional Indian sweet often served on special occasions.

w-in-018.title: Chana Masala

instructions.1: Soak the chickpeas in water with baking soda for at least 8 hours.
instructions.2: Drain the chickpeas and place them in a pressure cooker with 3 cups of water and 1 teaspoon of salt. Cook for 10 minutes.
instructions.3: In a pan, toast coriander seeds, cumin, pepper, clove, black cardamom, cinnamon, mace, fennel, shah jeera, and dried red chilli. Grind them to make chana masala powder.
instructions.4: In another pan, melt the ghee and add cinnamon, black cardamom, bay leaf, and cumin. Sauté the onions until golden brown.
instructions.5: Add the slit chilli, ginger garlic paste, turmeric, and tomato puree. Cook for 5 minutes.
instructions.6: Add the cooked chickpeas and 1 teaspoon of salt. Cook for 10 minutes.
instructions.7: Add the chana masala powder and coriander. Cook for an additional 5 minutes.
instructions.8: Serve the chana masala hot with rice or roti.

w-in-018.culturalNotes: Chana masala is a popular dish in Indian cuisine, typically served with rice or roti.

w-in-019.title: Chapati

instructions.1: Knead the flour and water together, starting with a small amount of water and adding more gradually until the dough becomes smooth but not too sticky.
instructions.2: Cover the dough and let it rest for at least 5 minutes.
instructions.3: Divide the dough into small balls and roll them out into disks, slightly thicker than denim fabric; sprinkle with flour as you roll.
instructions.4: Place a non-oiled pan over moderately high heat and test its surface temperature by holding your hand over it.
instructions.5: When the pan is very hot, place a chapati on it and press it flat with a spatula or dry cloth to make it rise up.
instructions.6: Flip the chapati and repeat the process until it is lightly browned on both sides.
instructions.7: If desired, brush the chapati with ghee.

w-in-019.culturalNotes: Chapati is a traditional Indian flatbread served with many main dishes.

w-in-020.title: Chhena Poda

instructions.1: Pour the milk into a pan and bring it to a boil over medium heat.
instructions.2: Add the lemon juice and stir gently until the milk starts to curdle.
instructions.3: Strain the curdled milk using a clean cloth and rinse it with cold water for a few minutes.
instructions.4: Add the sugar, semolina, and water, and mix well.
instructions.5: Add the cashews, pistachios, cinnamon, and cloves, and mix again.
instructions.6: Strain the mixture once more using a clean cloth and let it dry for 30 minutes.
instructions.7: Place the mixture in a greased baking dish and bake in a preheated oven at 180°C for one hour.
instructions.8: Let the chhena poda cool before serving.

w-in-020.culturalNotes: Chhena Poda is a traditional Indian sweet from the state of Odisha, known for its rich and delicious flavor.

w-in-021.title: Instant Pot Chicken Tikka Masala

w-in-021-i14.name: chopped tomatoes
w-in-021-i14.standardAmount: 3 plum tomatoes or 1.5 cups diced or pureed tomatoes

instructions.1: Make 2-3 slits in the chicken breasts. Apply salt and lemon juice to the chicken breasts. Mix yogurt, Kashmiri red chili powder, garam masala, ginger, and garlic. Apply the mixture evenly to the chicken breasts and let it marinate for 20 minutes or refrigerate if marinating ahead of time.
instructions.2: Set the Instant Pot to Saute mode and heat butter or oil. Add onions and sauté for 2 minutes. Add ginger, garlic, and mix well. Add tomatoes, turmeric, salt, Kashmiri red chili powder, and garam masala. Mix well. Press Cancel. Add 2 tablespoons of water. Deglaze the pot if needed.
instructions.3: Place the tall trivet in the main pot. Place the marinated chicken over the trivet. Baste the chicken with oil. Close the Instant Pot with the pressure valve to sealing. Pressure Cook for 8 minutes followed by a 10-minute natural pressure release.
instructions.4: Open the Instant Pot. Take the chicken and the trivet out. Use an immersion blender to blend the sauce until smooth.
instructions.5: Stir in the cream and kasoori methi.
instructions.6: Broil the cooked chicken in a preheated oven for 5 minutes to get some char marks (optional). Cut the chicken into 2-inch pieces and add them to the sauce.
instructions.7: Set the Instant Pot to sauté mode and bring the curry to a gentle boil. The sauce will thicken further as it cools down. Garnish with cilantro.

w-in-021.culturalNotes: Chicken Tikka Masala is a famous Indian dish, known for its garam masala, cream, and dried fenugreek leaves flavors.

w-in-022.title: Chicken Tikka

w-in-022-i9.name: Chopped fresh red chillis
w-in-022-i9.standardAmount: 1-4 (depending on strength of the chillis and the desired strength of the marinade)

w-in-022-i14.name: Salt
w-in-022-i14.standardAmount: 1 tsp (use rock salt for best results)

instructions.1: Add all of the ingredients except the chicken to a non-metallic mixing bowl, and mix well.
instructions.2: Add the chicken and mix until fully coated.
instructions.3: Ideally, the chicken should be left in a refrigerator to marinate for at least 24 hours. Fresh chicken should be left to marinate for 48 hours for best results.
instructions.4: Place the chicken on skewers and cook in a tandoor or ceramic pot oven. The chicken can also be cooked on skewers under a medium grill for 5-8 minutes on each side or barbecued (cooking times depend on the temperature of the barbecue). Always ensure the chicken is cooked throughout before serving.

w-in-022.culturalNotes: Chicken tikka is a popular dish in Indian cuisine, typically served with naan, rice, or used in Chicken Tikka Masala.
